Camera at standing height a few paces back from the near machine and offset well to one side, so the machine bank runs across the frame obliquely and the room stacks up behind it.
A low frame from about waist height, close in beside the near machine's flank so that flank rakes away down one side of the picture and the rest of the row opens at an angle beyond it.
Camera set three-quarters to the near machine from its front corner so one long side recedes into the picture and the row past it sits smaller.
From a little above head height and offset to one side, angled down across the width of the row so the near tops stay sharp and the far end softens.
A frame from close off to one side, the near glass crossing the lower two thirds and running out of both side edges, the enclosing surfaces in a band above it.
Camera set low near the floor a couple of paces out, tilted slightly up, the near machine large down one side and the room opening obliquely past it.
From just past one tall upright at the extreme near edge — a mirrored column, a post or a machine's own corner — its mass down one side of the frame and everything else open at an angle beyond it.
A frame taken from behind and to one side of a low glass-topped machine, looking across its top obliquely so the top runs out of frame and the room rises behind.
Camera at chest height set at an oblique angle into a turning-space, both ranks falling away to either side rather than ahead.
From high up under the close ceiling, just below whatever crosses it, so that crossing mass cuts the top of the frame and the room opens obliquely below it.
A frame from standing height close in and offset, the near glass turned three-quarters on and filling the lower half, the enclosing side surfaces bracketing it.
Camera low and close to the polished floor a few steps off, angled up and across so the floor's reflections fill the bottom and the row leans over obliquely.
From one end of a short bay, offset from its centre line and turned, so the bay's far corner sits in one third of the frame rather than dead ahead.
A slightly raised frame set off the row's long axis, high enough that both the near tops and the far corner read, with the near machine filling one side.
Camera set just inside an opening at the near side, the opening's dark edge across one side of the frame and the room beyond it at an angle.
From behind something low running across the near edge — a rail, a bench or a step — it running away obliquely across the bottom of the frame and the machines standing past it.
A tight three-quarter frame on the near machine from slightly below, its top band and the close ceiling above it both in shot, the row falling away behind to one side.
Camera placed to one side of whatever stands at the near edge — a stack of stools, a post or a crate — just past it, the room falling away behind at an angle.

From standing height beside a shoulder-high surface with things crowded along its top — a partition, a counter or a low bank of machines — looking across that top obliquely so it runs off one edge and the far surfaces stand beyond.
A frame from a couple of paces off and well to one side, the near machine's glass still filling one whole side of the picture and the room's surfaces layered above and beyond it.
Camera at head height turned hard to one side so the row runs out of the left of the frame and an enclosing surface closes the right.
From above a glass top at close range and offset, angled down across it so the glass fills a corner and the room opens obliquely past it.

A frame from a raised spot at the room's edge — a stair head, a wide step, a landing or a rail — turned and looking obliquely across the floor so the machines run crosswise below and the ceiling closes overhead.
Camera set low between two machines and offset from the gap's centre, one flank raking down each side and the space beyond opening at an angle.
A medium frame at standing height from the near corner of the floor, everything turned three-quarters so no surface faces us squarely.
From the far end of the row looking back along it, offset from the centre line and turned slightly, so the machines recede in perspective down one side and the ceiling drops toward them.
A frame shot from a crouching position in the gap between two rows, the flanks of both rising on either side and the far end of the aisle opening obliquely ahead.
Camera placed at the very corner where two ranks meet at a right angle, turned to split the frame between the two directions so each row falls away into its own depth.
From just below the level of a machine's coin tray, close and offset, the tray's underside cutting across the upper third and the polished side filling one edge of the picture.
A wide frame taken from the far end of the room, standing height, the whole row running toward the camera along one side and the open floor filling the other.
Camera positioned at chest height inside a narrow cross-passage between banks, both openings visible at either edge and the machines walling the top and bottom of the frame.
From a slight elevation off to one side, the near row's tops receding at a sharp angle toward the back wall while the floor's surface stretches flat in the foreground below.
A frame taken from behind a glass panel set into a machine's side — that panel close and occupying one half — the reflected glow of the neighbouring screen caught in it.
Camera high and pressed into a far corner of the room, angled down and across so the whole floor spreads diagonally below and the near walls bracket either side.
From the side of a rounded-edge cabinet at very close range, the curve of that edge running vertically through the centre of the frame and the row continuing in soft depth behind it.
A frame set at knee height well behind the row, tilted up so the machines' backs face the lens and the ceiling above them is the picture's upper boundary.
Camera offset to one side at standing height beside a cluster of tall uprights, their closely spaced vertical forms filling half the frame and the open floor visible past them.
From a position close beside a low machine with a flat horizontal surface, that surface running out of the near edge and the taller cabinets rising in a rank beyond it.
A frame from shoulder height behind the furthest machine in the row, looking back toward the entrance so the row recedes away from the camera and the near opening sits at the far end.
Camera placed at standing height where a side wall meets the row's end, the wall surface filling the right of the frame and the row running away leftward at a slight angle.
From the floor level at the far corner of the room, angled up across the diagonal so the machines run from large at the near side to small at the distance.
A close frame from below the overhang of a machine's top hood, that hood cutting the sky of the image and the rank of machines behind sitting in the shadow beneath it.
Camera set at mid-height between two banks in a wide aisle, turned to favour one side so that bank fills three-quarters of the frame and the opposite bank sits as a thin strip.
From standing height at the edge of a shallow step running in front of the row, the step's edge crossing the lower third of the frame and the machines standing past it.
A frame taken from an angle where one machine's back panel and its neighbour's front glass both read at once, the seam between them running vertically through the near third of the picture.
Camera at head height a few paces past the row's end, turned back so the terminal machine's side fills the near edge and the ceiling runs away above in perspective.
From close range and well offset, looking into the gap between a machine and the side wall, that gap dark and narrow in one side of the frame and the open room on the other.
A frame from a high shelf or narrow ledge at the room's edge, looking obliquely downward so the ledge's surface crosses the near foreground and the floor below opens past it.
Camera set at waist height behind a low partition running parallel to the row, that partition's top edge crossing the frame and the machines standing above it in the distance.
From the centre of the room at standing height, turned so the two converging rows form a wide V shape receding away, the apex sitting in the upper middle of the frame.
Camera at standing height set just past the end of the row looking back along it, the machines receding into the far corner and the ceiling dropping away with them.
From the far end of the room, a long frame along the wall so the row lines one side of the picture and the open floor fills the other, both shrinking toward the back.
A frame from mid-height between two rows facing each other, the near flanks on either side raking inward and the aisle between them pulling back into the room.
Camera high and centred above the aisle, aimed steeply down so the tops form two parallel bands either side and the floor strip between them runs back to the far wall.
From just inside the far corner of the room, turned so both enclosing walls sit in shot and the machines stand out from them at an angle into the open space.
A close frame from chest height aimed into the angle where two rows meet at a corner, both flanks running away from the near point in different directions.
Camera set level with the underside of an overhead fascia, that fascia cutting a dark band across the top and the machines ranked below it in even light.
From slightly above waist height and square to the gap between two machines, the gap itself a narrow bright slit and both flanks pressing in from either side.
A wide frame from the near wall looking across the room's short axis rather than its long one, the row running straight across the middle and the ceiling pressing close above.
Camera tilted gently up from just below the level of a tall machine's mid-point, the marquee area looming at the top and the lower cab receding into perspective below.
From a low stool-height position close off one end machine, the end panel flat on in the frame and the long row stepping back from it at full depth.
A frame taken from behind the far end of the row looking back toward the entrance, the machines in silhouette against the light beyond and the ceiling low overhead.
Camera placed in the narrow space between a machine and the wall behind it, the wall surface close across one side and the machine's back panel beside it, the room's edge just past.
From a raised corner bracket position, the two nearest ceiling edges meeting near one corner of the frame and the machines arranged across the floor below them at an angle.
A tight upward frame from very close in below a machine's marquee, the underside of the top housing filling the upper picture and the cabinet body falling away beneath it.
Camera at standing height looking obliquely along a row from behind its midpoint, half the machines ahead and half behind, both sets diminishing in opposite directions.
From a few paces back at head height, a machine pulled partly out of its row sits nearest, its flank exposed and the gap it leaves dark behind it.
A frame from the room's far wall at chest height, the full width of the floor between camera and nearest row visible so the floor reads as a wide foreground plane.
Camera just inside a low alcove set into one wall, the alcove's near edge framing the left side and a single machine filling the centre, the room behind it at an angle.
From directly behind and tight to a machine's back, looking over its top along the row ahead, the top's edge a hard line and the other machines stepping down beyond it.
A frame at standing height set close beside the joint where two bays meet at a right angle, the corner post centred and both bays falling away to either side of it.
Camera level with the top of a low glass-fronted cabinet from a pace back, the cabinet's top edge a horizontal band through the middle and the taller machines ranked behind it.
From the exact centre of the aisle at mid-height, the camera turned forty-five degrees so neither wall faces squarely and the machines on each side cut diagonally into the frame.
A slightly overhead frame aimed downward along the diagonal of the room's rectangle, so both a long side and a short side recede together toward the far corner.
Camera set just above floor level at the base of a tall machine's front, the cabinet rising steeply overhead and the row curving away in shallow perspective to one side.
From directly behind the far end of the row, the line of machine backs receding toward the near end and narrowing, the ceiling dropping in perspective above and the floor rising below.
A frame at standing height from the room's far corner, the two walls meeting just off-centre and the machines running along one of them toward the near edge of the picture.
Camera set level with the coin slots on the near machine, close enough that the slot panel fills the middle of the frame and the row recedes at a steep angle behind it.
From just above a waist-high machine top in the centre of the floor, looking along the gap between two rows so both inner flanks run away in parallel and the far wall closes the picture.
A wide frame taken from the room's near wall itself, the wall's own surface crossing the bottom edge and the machines standing away from it at a slight angle across the middle distance.
Camera tilted down from a point level with the overhead fixtures, their undersides crossing the top quarter and the row below them angled so the far end sits in one corner.
From a low crouch just past the near machine's base, angled upward along its full height so the cabinet towers and the ceiling appears above its top on one side.
A frame set at the mouth of a narrow passage between two bays, the passage's inner surfaces pressing in on both sides and the open floor of the main room visible at its far end.
Camera at chest height from the far corner of the room, looking back diagonally across the whole floor so all the rows read at once and the near machines fill the right foreground.
From one side of a ceiling-mounted light fitting, its casing cutting into the upper corner of the frame and the machines below it lit unevenly across the picture.
A close frame on the angled join between two machine banks meeting at a corner, both rows receding away from that joint at equal angles and the ceiling above the joint in shot.
Camera placed at the centre of the floor facing across the short axis of the room, the rows running left and right past frame rather than ahead, the far wall straight in front.
From beside a low platform or raised section of floor at the room's edge, its step edge crossing the near foreground diagonally and the machines standing on the lower level beyond it.
A frame taken from the top of a short flight of steps leading into the room, the steps descending in the near foreground and the machine row at the bottom running crosswise.
Camera set behind a glass panel, looking through it so the panel's surface gives a faint layering to the machines visible beyond and the room's far surfaces sit deep in the picture.
From a tight angle pressed close to the far wall, the wall's surface filling the right side of the frame and the machine row running away from it at an oblique angle to the left.
A frame from directly overhead, the tops of the machines in a grid below and the narrow aisles between them forming a pattern of lines across the picture.
Camera set at the far end of a single aisle, dead centre of the gap, the two flanking rows of cabinets forming a corridor that closes at the near end of the room.
From a mid-level position behind a curved glass surface, that curve bending through the foreground and the machines beyond it slightly distorted by the glass's shape.
A frame at waist height from the exact midpoint of the room's long axis, the rows spreading equally to either side and the near and far walls both just in shot.
Camera placed at floor level beneath a machine's overhanging marquee, the marquee's underside filling the top of the frame and the aisle floor stretching away below it.

From the hinge point of two rooms opening into one another, the near room's machines on one side and the far room's machines at a different angle on the other, the opening itself crossing the picture.
A frame at head height looking into a corner where two machine banks and the wall all converge, each surface meeting at a slightly different angle and the ceiling above the junction in shot.
Camera set well back at standing height with a shallow machine console in the immediate foreground, its surface crossing the very bottom of the frame and the taller cabinets standing behind it.
From a point just above the polished surface of a waist-high machine, level and close, so the surface acts as a near plane and the room's machines and walls rise beyond its far edge.
